Hi Emma, Rachel — thanks for looping me in. I wanted to provide a single-threaded technical summary you can share with Acme InfoSec; happy to go deeper on the call.

High-level attestation (summary):
- Redwood Inference will not use customer production input/output content to train or update our public model weights for hosted API customers by default. We will provide a signed attestation to that effect for Acme.
- Exceptions: explicit opt-in programs (e.g., research collaborations) are always documented and require an explicit contract amendment. No production customer data is included in opt-in training without customer consent.

Retention/Deletion overview (default hosted behavior):
- API request & response logs: retained for 30 days for debugging, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. After 30 days, logs are deleted from primary active stores and retained in a short-term snapshot for an additional 60 days only for incident response.
- Telemetry/metrics (aggregated): retained indefinitely in aggregated form; no PII is present.
- KV cache / session ephemeral state: ephemeral by design — not persisted across customer sessions for hosted customers unless the customer uses the Redwood-managed session store feature; even then data is isolated per-customer and not used for model training.
- Backups & disaster recovery snapshots: retained up to 180 days depending on region and legal hold policies; these backups are encrypted, access-controlled, and can be purged on customer request subject to business continuity considerations.

Deletion upon request:
- For hosted API customers, a standard deletion request will remove active logs and session data within 30 days and trigger a backup purge workflow which completes within 180 days.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments: data residency and retention follow the committed contract — Private (on-prem/VPC) customers own the data store and can apply their own deletion policies; Redwood’s control plane does not ingest customer row-level content for training.

No-training assurance details:
- We maintain a policy and engineering controls that segregate production data from model-training pipelines. Model training pipelines use curated public datasets, open models, and customer-approved opt-ins only.
- Engineering safeguards: tagged datasets, separation of credentials, and auditing are in place; we can provide an architectural diagram in the compliance pack.

Artifacts available for Acme:
- SOC 2 (scope doc) — available under NDA.
- Signed non-training attestation (we will provide a PDF).
- Data retention matrix (attached) mapping the fields in your spreadsheet to Redwood timelines and responsible teams.

Next steps / proposed meeting:
- Rachel: 10:00 PT on Wed 6/9 works for us.
- Emma: we'll bring the attestation PDF and the CSV mapping to the call and can answer any procurement redlines live.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
